title: A Static for the Colony
premise: Bram Joubert, a former insurance investigator turned cargo hauler in the contested orbits of Meridian Station, is hired to assess a claim on a decommissioned ore platform where records insist no one ever died. As the colony's children begin dreaming identical memories of a massacre that officially never happened, Bram discovers his own suppressed past is tangled with the erased event — he was there, and his testimony was bought and buried. Racing against a corporate wipe scheduled to scrub the last children's minds, Bram must choose between the quiet life he's built with station medic Yara Solenne and the duty of restoring truth, knowing proof will cost him everything. In the end he broadcasts the children's shared dream across every colony channel, sacrificing his ship, his clean record, and his chance at a life with Yara — but the colony remembers, and the ones responsible are finally named.
about_author: Ansel Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. Writing from a coastal town that floods a little more each year, they craft science fiction about ordinary people caught between paperwork and conscience.

chapters.title: The Claim That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Bram Joubert takes a routine damage claim on derelict Platform Kestrel-9, but the manifest lists zero casualties for an accident his instruments say killed forty people. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in a world built on tidy records.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Station medic Yara Solenne treats a cluster of children suffering identical nightmares: fire, airlocks, screaming in a language none of them speak. She asks Bram, as an investigator, to look. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread mixed with tenderness toward the frightened kids.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Bram digs into Kestrel-9's history and finds three years of records seamlessly rewritten — including a crew roster with his own name redacted. His hands shake; he doesn't know why. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: creeping self-doubt as memory and documents disagree.

chapters.title: What the Dream Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara hypnotically interviews one child, Mika, whose dream contains details only a survivor could know — including a man with a burned left hand. Bram looks at his own scarred hand. POV: Mika, then Bram. Emotional beat: horror of recognition.

chapters.title: The Buyer of Silence
chapters.summary: Bram traces hush-money payments to Halcyon Combine executive Dara Voss, who offers him a fortune to drop the claim — and reminds him he already sold his testimony once. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: shame curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: Yara's Choice
chapters.summary: Yara discovers the children are scheduled for 'cognitive hygiene screening' — a memory wipe disguised as vaccination. She must decide whether to break medical law and warn them. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: love against duty, choosing the children over her license.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9
chapters.summary: Bram and Yara board the dead platform and find sealed quarters, scorch marks, and a hidden recorder containing the massacre footage — with Bram's younger self testifying under duress. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief and self-forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Halcyon security traps them aboard; Yara is taken, and the recorder is seized — but Bram realizes the children's shared dream is itself a backup of the evidence. POV: alternating Bram/Yara. Emotional beat: despair hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Bram rams his cargo hauler through the station's comm array while Yara, escaped, guides the children to describe the dream live on every open channel. The massacre plays out in a thousand young voices. POV: both. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, terror, and terrible beauty.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Voss is arrested as the colony demands answers; the children's wipes are cancelled. Bram, stripped of his license and ship, stands with Yara at the dock — poorer, guilty, but finally whole. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; memory reclaimed, love chosen freely.
